title: TaylorMade P790 Irons in Kenya: The Complete Buyer’s Guide
excerpt: Considering TaylorMade P790 irons in Kenya? Understand the 2025 design, 4–PW set, shaft choices, flex options and checks to make before ordering.
author: Karibu Golf editorial team
cover_alt: TaylorMade P790 iron photographed for Karibu Golf in Kenya
seo_title: TaylorMade P790 Irons Kenya: 2025 Buyer’s Guide
meta_description: A Kenya-focused TaylorMade P790 irons guide covering the 2025 model, 4–PW set, steel and graphite shafts, flex choices, specifications and price checks.
content:
**The 2025 TaylorMade P790 is a players-distance iron for golfers who want a compact, premium-looking head with more speed and forgiveness than a traditional compact players iron.** Karibu Golf’s current listing is a seven-club 4–PW set with steel or graphite shaft choices and Regular, Stiff or Senior flex options; Senior is available with graphite only. [View the live TaylorMade P790 listing, current KSh price and availability](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/).

This guide explains what the specifications mean before you order. It is not a substitute for an in-person fitting, and it does not claim that one iron model is best for every golfer.

## P790 buyer summary

- **Category:** players-distance iron.
- **Karibu set:** 4-iron through pitching wedge, seven clubs.
- **Shaft choices:** steel or graphite, subject to exact stock confirmation.
- **Flex choices:** Regular and Stiff in steel; Regular, Stiff and Senior in graphite.
- **Best reason to consider it:** you prefer a cleaner players-style shape but still want useful speed and forgiveness.
- **Main check before paying:** confirm the exact shaft model, flex, handedness, set composition and photographs of the actual set.

## What changed in the 2025 TaylorMade P790?

TaylorMade describes the 2025 P790 as an individually optimised hollow-body iron with a forged 4340M face, SpeedFoam Air and FLTD CG. The manufacturer says the face material is stronger than the previous generation and uses that strength to support a larger effective sweet spot. Those are manufacturer design claims, not a promise that every golfer will gain a particular distance.

FLTD CG means the centre of gravity changes progressively through the set. The long irons are designed around easier launch and speed, while the shorter irons move toward controlled flight and scoring. That matters because a seven-club iron set should not feel like seven copies of the same head. Each club has a different job.

TaylorMade also lists a thinner topline, an increased sole radius and a progressive leading edge. In practical terms, those details shape how the club looks at address and moves through the turf. Your delivery and course conditions still influence the result.

## Is the P790 forgiving?

TaylorMade places the P790 between its game-improvement irons and more compact players irons. In its own P-Series comparison, the P790 is described as players distance with mid-high forgiveness, mid-high trajectory, mid workability and long distance.

That makes it more forgiving on paper than models built primarily for shot shaping, but it is not the company’s highest-forgiveness iron. A golfer who strikes the face inconsistently should compare it with a larger game-improvement head rather than buying from appearance alone.

The useful question is not simply, “Is it forgiving?” Ask, “Does it give me acceptable launch, carry and dispersion when I miss the centre?” That requires hitting shots or working with a qualified fitter where possible.

## What is included in the Karibu 4–PW set?

The current Karibu listing includes 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 irons plus a pitching wedge. Manufacturer reference lofts for the 2025 model are 20°, 23°, 26.5°, 30°, 34°, 39° and 44° respectively.

A 4–PW set does not include an approach wedge or sand wedge. TaylorMade lists a 49° approach wedge in the wider P790 family, but it is not part of this seven-club Karibu set unless the listing explicitly says otherwise. Review your wedge setup after the 44° pitching wedge so there is no accidental distance gap.

If you struggle to launch a 4-iron, ask whether a hybrid should fill that part of the bag. Owning the full set does not obligate you to use every iron in every round.

## Steel or graphite P790 shafts?

Steel often appeals to players who prefer a more substantial feel and consistent feedback. Graphite can reduce total shaft weight and may feel easier to swing for some golfers. Neither material is automatically more accurate, more advanced or more suitable for a particular age.

The exact model and weight matter as much as the material label. TaylorMade lists multiple manufacturer configurations, including steel and graphite options with different weights and launch profiles. Karibu will confirm what is fitted to the actual set before payment. Read our detailed [steel versus graphite iron shaft guide](/blog/steel-vs-graphite-iron-shafts-kenya/) before choosing.

## Which flex should you choose?

Regular, Stiff and Senior are not scores for how good a golfer is. They describe shaft families, and the labels are not perfectly standardised between manufacturers. Tempo, transition, delivery, strike and preferred feel all matter.

As a starting point, choose the flex you can deliver repeatedly without forcing speed. A player with a forceful transition may prefer a different response from a player with the same clubhead speed and a smooth tempo. If you are uncertain, do not guess from age or handicap; ask for the shaft model and seek fitting advice. Our [Regular versus Stiff versus Senior flex guide](/blog/regular-stiff-senior-iron-flex-guide/) explains the decision in more detail.

## What should you confirm when buying P790 irons in Kenya?

1. Ask for the exact model year and SKU. P790 generations have different specifications.
2. Confirm every included club in writing. “P790 set” is not enough.
3. Confirm right- or left-handed orientation.
4. Request the shaft manufacturer, model, material, weight and flex.
5. Ask whether length, lie or loft has been altered.
6. Request current photographs of the actual heads, faces, shafts and grips.
7. Confirm the final KSh price, delivery cost, payment process and seller terms.
8. Keep the written specification with your order.

The [live Karibu P790 product page](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) shows current stock and price. Use the configurator to send your preferred hand, shaft and flex by WhatsApp. A selection is an enquiry preference; Karibu confirms the exact item before payment.

## Is the P790 worth the price?

Value depends on whether the specification solves your actual equipment need. The P790 combines a premium construction, a compact profile and distance-oriented engineering, but none of that creates value if the shaft, set makeup or launch does not suit you.

Compare the final delivered price with the exact configuration—not an overseas headline price before shipping, taxes or support. Then compare performance: carry gaps, height, front-to-back dispersion, left-to-right dispersion and your confidence at address. A less expensive iron that fits can be better value than a premium iron chosen only by name.

## Who should consider a P790 fitting?

Consider trying the P790 if you:

- Prefer a refined head shape rather than an oversized game-improvement look.
- Want more speed and help on imperfect contact than a traditional compact players iron.
- Need a full 4–PW iron set and understand how it fits around your hybrids and wedges.
- Are willing to choose the shaft and flex deliberately.
- Care about both distance and predictable gapping.

Compare other categories first if maximum forgiveness is your only priority, if you cannot launch the longer irons, or if a smaller partial set would suit your budget and game better.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much do TaylorMade P790 irons cost in Kenya?

The current Karibu price is shown in KSh on the [live P790 product page](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/). Check the page rather than relying on an old article price because exchange rates, stock and configurations can change. Confirm delivery and the exact set before payment.

### Are P790 irons for beginners?

Some developing golfers may enjoy them, but they are not automatically the best beginner iron. TaylorMade positions the P790 as players distance, not as its maximum-forgiveness model. A beginner should compare contact, launch and dispersion with a game-improvement option.

### Is the P790 forged?

TaylorMade describes the 2025 model as using a forged 4340M face within a hollow-body construction. “Forged” does not mean it is a one-piece traditional blade.

### Does the Karibu P790 set include a sand wedge?

No. The listed set is 4–PW. Ask separately about wedges that create useful loft and carry gaps below the 44° pitching wedge.

### Can I order graphite Senior flex?

Yes, the Karibu configurator includes Senior flex when graphite is selected. Exact shaft model and availability must still be confirmed.

title: Steel vs Graphite Iron Shafts: A Practical Guide for Kenyan Golfers
excerpt: Steel or graphite iron shafts? Compare weight, feel, launch, consistency and fitting questions before choosing your next iron set in Kenya.
author: Karibu Golf editorial team
cover_alt: TaylorMade P790 iron profile with shaft visible
seo_title: Steel vs Graphite Iron Shafts: Kenya Buyer’s Guide
meta_description: Compare steel and graphite iron shafts for weight, feel, launch and control. A practical Kenya buying guide using the TaylorMade P790 as an example.
content:
**Choose an iron shaft by its total weight, flex profile, length, balance and how consistently you deliver it—not by material alone.** Steel usually offers a familiar, substantial feel and many weight choices; graphite can be lighter and may reduce transmitted vibration. Either can perform well when it fits the golfer.

Karibu’s [TaylorMade P790 listing](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) offers steel and graphite selections, making it a useful real-world example. This guide helps you ask the right questions before ordering in Kenya.

## The short answer

Choose **steel** if you prefer its feel, find a weight you can repeat and see better strike and dispersion with it. Choose **graphite** if a lighter build, different feel or reduced vibration helps you swing and strike the ball more consistently. Do not choose graphite only because of age, or steel only because stronger players use it.

Two shafts made from the same material can behave very differently. Always get the exact manufacturer, model, weight and flex.

## What changes when you change shaft material?

The shaft is part of the club’s delivery system. Changing it can alter total weight, balance, how the club loads during the swing, impact feel and the golfer’s timing. It may also change launch and spin, but the result is personal rather than guaranteed.

A shaft does not independently create a good ball flight. Clubhead design, loft, length, lie, strike location, speed and delivery all contribute. That is why a material-only comparison is incomplete.

## Why golfers choose steel iron shafts

Steel shafts are common in iron sets because they can provide:

- A stable and familiar feel for many players.
- A wide range of weights and flex profiles.
- Clear feedback about strike location.
- Consistent manufacturing at many price points.
- A build that some golfers find easier to sense throughout the swing.

The tradeoff is that a heavier steel option may tire a player or make it harder to create comfortable speed. Steel can also transmit more impact vibration than some graphite constructions. Those are tendencies, not universal outcomes. Modern lightweight steel and heavier graphite overlap, so “steel is heavy” and “graphite is light” are not complete rules.

## Why golfers choose graphite iron shafts

Graphite shafts can provide:

- Lower total weight in many available models.
- A smoother or different impact sensation.
- Reduced vibration for some players.
- More design freedom for weight and bend profile.
- An option for golfers who maintain better tempo and contact with a lighter club.

Graphite is not automatically soft, inconsistent or only for slow swings. Premium graphite iron shafts are made in a wide range of weights and profiles. The important question is whether the exact model gives you repeatable contact and useful ball flight.

## Does graphite always launch higher?

No. Shaft makers can design both steel and graphite models for different launch windows. A lighter graphite shaft may help one golfer launch the ball higher because they deliver more speed or dynamic loft, while another golfer may see little change.

Treat launch descriptions such as low, mid or high as comparison guidance within a manufacturer’s range, not a guaranteed flight. The clubhead and golfer still matter.

## How shaft weight affects your irons

Weight is often more useful than the steel-versus-graphite label. A shaft that is too heavy may make it difficult to complete the swing or maintain contact late in a round. A shaft that feels too light may reduce awareness of the clubhead or disrupt tempo.

When comparing, hit enough shots to get past the excitement of the first few swings. Note:

1. Centre-contact frequency.
2. Carry-distance consistency.
3. Left-to-right dispersion.
4. Peak height and landing angle.
5. How your tempo feels.
6. Whether effort increases after several swings.

The best result is the setup you can repeat, not the single longest shot.

## Steel vs graphite in the TaylorMade P790

TaylorMade lists the 2025 P790 with several steel and graphite configurations, depending on market and custom availability. The head remains a players-distance design, but the shaft can materially change total club feel.

On Karibu’s product page, choosing Steel shows Regular and Stiff flex. Choosing Graphite shows Regular, Stiff and Senior. The Senior option is intentionally restricted to graphite so the order enquiry matches the available configuration logic.

Before paying, ask Karibu to confirm:

- Exact shaft brand and model.
- Shaft material and stated weight.
- Flex printed on the shaft.
- Club length and whether it is standard or altered.
- Right- or left-handed head.
- The seven included clubs.
- Photographs of the actual set.

Use the [P790 product configurator](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) to send your preferred setup, then wait for exact stock confirmation.

## What if you have elbow, wrist or shoulder discomfort?

Some golfers prefer the vibration-damping feel of graphite, but equipment is not medical treatment. Pain can come from technique, practice volume, an injury or several other causes. Stop if a swing hurts and seek appropriate medical or coaching advice.

If you return to play, compare complete club builds rather than assuming any graphite shaft will solve discomfort. Grip size, club length, swing weight and impact quality also affect feel.

## Does Kenya’s weather change the choice?

Normal Kenyan playing conditions do not create a rule that one shaft material is required. Heat, rain and humidity can affect grip, comfort and course conditions, but shaft selection still comes back to fit and repeatability.

Maintain the clubs properly: dry them after wet rounds, inspect grips, avoid leaving equipment in extreme heat for long periods and use a bag that protects shafts from repeated impact.

## A simple decision process

1. Start with a comfortable total weight.
2. Compare at least one steel and one graphite option if available.
3. Keep head model, loft and length as similar as possible during the comparison.
4. Judge a group of shots, not the best shot.
5. Check carry gaps and dispersion.
6. Confirm the exact shaft in the set you will receive.
7. Choose the option that makes a repeatable swing feel natural.

If you cannot test, be conservative. Use a specification you already know, ask detailed questions and avoid buying from a flex label alone.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are graphite iron shafts better for senior golfers?

They can be useful because many graphite models are lighter and damp vibration, but age does not determine the correct shaft. Strength, tempo, delivery, contact and comfort matter more.

### Do professional golfers use graphite iron shafts?

Some do, while many use steel. Professional usage does not determine what fits a recreational golfer. Choose from your own results.

### Are steel shafts more accurate?

Not automatically. Accuracy depends on the complete club and golfer. A shaft that improves face contact and delivery can tighten dispersion regardless of material.

### Can I choose Senior flex in a steel P790 set from Karibu?

The current Karibu selector offers Senior flex with graphite only. Steel shows Regular and Stiff. Ask the team if you need a configuration not shown.

### Should every iron have the same shaft?

Most matched sets use the same shaft family with progressive club lengths, but specialist mixed builds exist. Do not create a mixed set casually; check weight, balance and distance gaps with a fitter.

- [Karibu Golf: live P790 shaft and flex selector](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/)
- [TaylorMade: P-Series iron comparison](https://www.taylormadegolf.com/P%E2%88%99790-Irons/DW-TC635.html?lang=en_US)

Manufacturer configurations and Karibu options checked 29 September 2026. Exact shafts can vary by market and stock.

title: Regular, Stiff or Senior Flex? How to Choose an Iron Shaft
excerpt: Regular, Stiff and Senior flex labels are a starting point—not a verdict. Learn how tempo, delivery, shaft weight and ball flight should guide your choice.
author: Karibu Golf editorial team
cover_alt: TaylorMade P790 iron viewed from the playing position with shaft attached
seo_title: Regular vs Stiff vs Senior Iron Flex: Kenya Guide
meta_description: Choose between Regular, Stiff and Senior iron shaft flex using tempo, delivery, strike and ball flight—not age or handicap. Includes P790 ordering advice.
content:
**Regular, Stiff and Senior flex are manufacturer labels for how a shaft is designed to load and recover; they are not universal measurements and they do not describe a golfer’s ability.** Choose flex together with shaft model and weight, then confirm the choice through contact, carry, dispersion and feel.

Karibu’s [TaylorMade P790 page](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) offers Regular and Stiff with steel, plus Regular, Stiff and Senior with graphite. Here is how to make that selection more intelligently.

## The quickest useful answer

- **Regular flex:** a common starting point for golfers with a smoother or moderate delivery, but the label alone is not a fitting.
- **Stiff flex:** can suit golfers who load the shaft more forcefully or prefer a firmer response, but it is not reserved for low handicaps.
- **Senior flex:** often appears in lighter graphite builds and may suit golfers who deliver the club more comfortably with a softer profile; age is not the deciding factor.

There is no reliable universal swing-speed boundary that works across every iron shaft brand. One company’s Regular can feel different from another company’s Regular.

## What does shaft flex actually affect?

During the swing, a shaft bends in more than one direction. Its overall stiffness, bend profile, torque, weight, length and balance interact with the golfer’s tempo and release. The flex word printed near the grip summarises only part of that design.

A well-matched shaft can make it easier to deliver the club consistently. A poor match can feel difficult to time, but the same symptom can also come from technique, length, lie, swing weight or the clubhead. Do not diagnose flex from one ball flight.

## Regular flex: who should test it?

Regular is a sensible comparison point for many recreational golfers. Test it if you have a controlled transition, value a responsive feel or do not know your current specification.

Regular is not automatically weak or inaccurate. In the right model and weight, it can be stable enough for an athletic swing. Conversely, a Regular shaft can still feel demanding if it is too heavy or has a profile that does not suit your delivery.

Judge the pattern. If Regular gives comfortable effort, predictable height and tight carry gaps, there is no reason to reject it because another player uses Stiff.

## Stiff flex: who should test it?

Stiff can be worth testing if you have a quick transition, load the shaft forcefully, prefer a firmer sensation or see better control with that profile. It may also appeal to a golfer whose current shaft feels difficult to time because it responds too much for their delivery.

Do not use Stiff as a status symbol. A shaft that demands extra effort can reduce speed, launch and centre contact. The goal is not to prove that you can swing it; the goal is to produce useful iron shots repeatedly.

## Senior flex: what does it mean?

Senior flex—often marked A—is generally softer than Regular within the same shaft family. It is frequently offered in graphite and may be paired with a lighter overall build. It can suit golfers who create better rhythm, height and contact with that response.

The name is imperfect. A younger golfer may fit Senior, and an older golfer may fit Regular or Stiff. Physical age does not measure tempo or delivery. Treat Senior as a product specification, not a judgement.

Karibu currently shows Senior only after Graphite is selected on the P790 page. If you switch back to Steel, the configurator returns to the steel-compatible Regular or Stiff choices.

## Why swing speed is not enough

Swing speed is useful information, but two golfers with similar speed can load the shaft differently. One may build speed gradually; the other may change direction aggressively. They can prefer different weights and profiles.

A proper comparison looks at:

- Club speed and ball speed.
- Strike location on the face.
- Launch, spin and peak height.
- Carry distance and front-to-back dispersion.
- Left-to-right dispersion.
- Tempo, effort and confidence.

Without a launch monitor, you can still compare contact marks, carry windows and shot pattern on a range. Use several shots per option and include imperfect strikes.

## Signs a flex may not suit you

These are reasons to investigate, not final proof:

- You must swing unusually hard to feel the club work.
- The club feels difficult to locate during the swing.
- Contact becomes less centred than with another option.
- Launch is consistently too low or too high for useful carry.
- Carry distance varies more than expected.
- The shot pattern widens even when your swing feels normal.
- You dislike the impact sensation enough to change your motion.

Check shaft weight, club length, lie and head model before blaming flex alone.

## How to choose a P790 flex

Start with the material you want to compare. Steel and graphite P790 builds can have different weights and balance, so a Regular steel shaft is not simply the same thing as a Regular graphite shaft in another material.

Then follow this process:

1. Confirm the exact shaft model in each available set.
2. Compare a familiar flex first.
3. Test one adjacent flex without changing your swing on purpose.
4. Record carry and dispersion across several shots.
5. Prefer repeatable contact over one fast result.
6. Check the longest and shortest irons, not only the 7-iron.
7. Confirm the chosen specification in writing before ordering.

If you cannot test the exact set, share your current iron model, shaft label, typical 7-iron carry, usual shot shape and what you want to change with Karibu. That information is more useful than saying only, “I need Stiff.”

## Flex and the seven-club 4–PW set

The same shaft family normally runs through the complete iron set, while club length and head specifications change. A flex that feels acceptable in a short iron may feel demanding in a 4-iron. That is one reason to test more than a 7-iron when possible.

The 2025 P790 also uses progressive head engineering through the set. Shaft choice should support that gapping rather than create a flight you cannot control at one end of the bag. Read [what 4–PW means](/blog/4-pw-iron-set-explained/) before choosing the full configuration.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Stiff flex more accurate than Regular?

No flex is automatically more accurate. The best option is the one that helps you deliver the face and strike consistently. Dispersion testing is more useful than the label.

### Should a beginner use Regular flex?

Regular is a common starting point, not a beginner rule. A beginner still needs suitable weight, length and head design. Try options with guidance when possible.

### Is Senior flex only for older golfers?

No. Senior is a shaft category, often in lighter graphite models. Choose it from delivery and results rather than date of birth.

### Can a fast golfer use graphite?

Yes. Graphite shafts are available in many weights and profiles. Material does not set a speed limit.

### Does Karibu offer X-Stiff P790 irons?

X-Stiff is not shown in the current Karibu P790 selector. The listed choices are Regular and Stiff in steel, and Regular, Stiff and Senior in graphite. Ask the team about special requirements.

## Sources and verification

- [TaylorMade: official 2025 P790 shaft and product specifications](https://www.taylormadegolf.com/P%E2%88%99790-Irons/DW-TC635.html?lang=en_US)
- [Karibu Golf: live P790 configuration options](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/)
- [TaylorMade: official P-Series iron comparison](https://www.taylormadegolf.com/P%E2%88%99790-Irons/DW-TC635.html?lang=en_US)

Options and product information checked 29 September 2026. Flex labels vary by shaft manufacturer and model.

title: What Does 4–PW Mean? Golf Iron Set Makeup Explained
excerpt: A 4–PW iron set contains seven clubs, but it does not include every wedge. Learn the lofts, gaps and extra clubs to consider before buying in Kenya.
author: Karibu Golf editorial team
cover_alt: TaylorMade P790 iron cavity representing a 4 through pitching wedge set
seo_title: What Does 4–PW Mean? Golf Iron Sets Explained
meta_description: A 4–PW golf iron set has seven clubs: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and pitching wedge. Learn P790 lofts, wedge gaps and what else your bag may need.
keywords: how many irons in a set
content:
**A 4–PW iron set contains seven clubs: the 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 irons plus a pitching wedge.** It does not normally include a 3-iron, approach wedge, gap wedge, sand wedge or lob wedge unless the product listing names them separately.

Karibu’s current [TaylorMade P790 set](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) is listed as 4–PW. Understanding that notation prevents one of the most common online golf-equipment mistakes: assuming “a full iron set” fills every distance in the bag.

## Exactly which clubs are in 4–PW?

A standard 4–PW listing should include:

1. 4-iron.
2. 5-iron.
3. 6-iron.
4. 7-iron.
5. 8-iron.
6. 9-iron.
7. Pitching wedge.

Count the individual clubs, not the numbers printed in a headline. Before paying, ask the seller to write the set makeup on the invoice or order message.

## The 2025 P790 loft progression

For the 2025 TaylorMade P790, the manufacturer’s reference lofts are:

- **4-iron:** 20°.
- **5-iron:** 23°.
- **6-iron:** 26.5°.
- **7-iron:** 30°.
- **8-iron:** 34°.
- **9-iron:** 39°.
- **Pitching wedge:** 44°.

TaylorMade also lists a 49° approach wedge in the wider family, but that club is outside the current Karibu 4–PW set. Model years differ, so do not apply these lofts to every older P790 generation.

Loft numbers help explain the design, but your real carry distances depend on speed, strike, launch, spin, conditions and the ball. Measure actual carry after receiving or testing a set.

## Why modern set labels can be confusing

Two pitching wedges from different iron models can have different lofts. One golfer’s 7-iron may also have the same loft as another model’s 6-iron. That means club numbers alone cannot tell you the distance gap.

When comparing iron sets, check:

- The loft of each club.
- The longest and shortest included club.
- Shaft, length and lie specifications.
- Your measured carry with each club.
- The loft and carry of the next club above and below the set.

This protects you from buying a set that looks complete on paper but leaves a large gap near the green or overlaps a hybrid.

## Do you need a 4-iron?

Not every golfer launches a 4-iron consistently. A 20° P790 4-iron can produce useful distance for the right player, but some golfers get better height and forgiveness from a hybrid or higher-loft fairway wood.

Compare the 4-iron with the longest alternative in your bag. Keep the one that gives you a useful combination of carry, stopping power and confidence. A low shot that runs far is not automatically better if you need the ball to hold a green.

You can still buy a 4–PW set and decide which clubs enter the bag for a particular course. The Rules of Golf set a maximum of fourteen clubs during a round; they do not require every club you own to be carried.

## What wedges do you need after a 44° pitching wedge?

Start with carry distance, not a fashionable number of wedges. The aim is to create playable gaps for full and partial shots. With a 44° pitching wedge, a golfer might investigate one or more wedges with higher lofts, but the correct spacing depends on the actual lofts and carry distances.

Ask these questions:

1. How far do I carry the pitching wedge on a normal full swing?
2. What is the loft and carry of my next wedge?
3. Is the gap too large for the shots I face?
4. Do I prefer full swings or partial wedge shots?
5. What bounce and sole design suit my delivery and usual turf or sand?

Do not buy a wedge from loft alone. Bounce, grind, head design, shaft and technique matter around the green. Browse the [Karibu wedge category](/shop/clubs/wedges/) as stock is added, and ask the team to confirm specifications.

## 4–PW vs 5–PW: which is better?

A 5–PW set contains six clubs and leaves the longest-iron position open. It can suit a golfer who already uses a hybrid instead of a 4-iron. A 4–PW set provides the matching 4-iron and gives you the option to test it.

Compare total cost and the top of your bag. If you already own a reliable hybrid that covers the 4-iron distance, a 5–PW option may avoid duplication. If you like long irons or want a consistent iron profile through that distance, 4–PW may be more useful.

The current Karibu P790 listing is 4–PW, so confirm all seven clubs are present before ordering.

## What else is needed to build a complete golf bag?

Irons cover only part of the bag. Depending on your game, you may also need:

- A driver for tee shots.
- Fairway woods or hybrids for longer distances.
- Additional wedges below the pitching wedge.
- A putter.
- A golf bag and basic accessories.

You do not need to reach fourteen. Build around distinct jobs and useful distance gaps. The [R&A equipment rule](https://www.randa.org/en/rog/the-rules-of-golf/rule-4) allows a maximum of fourteen clubs but permits fewer.

## Buying a 4–PW set online in Kenya

Before payment, request:

- A current photograph showing all seven heads.
- Close-ups of faces, grooves, soles and shafts.
- Right- or left-handed confirmation.
- Shaft material, model, weight and flex.
- Standard or altered length and lie.
- Grip condition.
- Final KSh price and delivery cost.
- Written seller terms.

On Karibu’s [live P790 page](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/), select hand, steel or graphite, and flex before sending the WhatsApp enquiry. Karibu then confirms the exact set and availability.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many clubs are in a 4–PW set?

Seven: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 irons plus the pitching wedge.

### Does 4–PW include a sand wedge?

No. A sand wedge would normally be listed separately as SW. Never assume it is included.

### Does P790 4–PW include an approach wedge?

Not in the current Karibu listing. TaylorMade publishes a 49° AW specification, but the listed Karibu set ends at the 44° pitching wedge.

### Is a 4-iron harder to hit than a hybrid?

Many golfers find a hybrid easier to launch, but results differ. Compare carry, height, dispersion and confidence.

### Can I play golf with only seven irons and a putter?

You can play with fewer than fourteen clubs, subject to the Rules and competition conditions. A practical bag should cover tee shots, longer approaches, short shots and putting, so most golfers add other club types.

## Sources and verification

title: What Are Players-Distance Irons? TaylorMade P790 Technology Explained
excerpt: Players-distance irons combine a cleaner shape with speed and forgiveness technology. See how the 2025 P790 uses a forged face, hollow body and progressive CG.
author: Karibu Golf editorial team
cover_alt: TaylorMade P790 iron positioned beside a golf ball on the course
meta_description: What are players-distance irons? Learn how the TaylorMade P790 combines a compact shape, hollow body, forged face, SpeedFoam Air and progressive CG.
content:
**Players-distance irons combine a cleaner, more compact appearance with construction intended to produce more ball speed and forgiveness than a traditional one-piece compact players iron.** The TaylorMade P790 is a prominent example: TaylorMade positions the 2025 model between its game-improvement irons and more compact P-Series players irons.

That category description is useful, but it does not guarantee a personal result. This guide explains the engineering claims so you can evaluate the [P790 available from Karibu Golf](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) with better questions.

## Players iron, game-improvement iron and players-distance iron

A traditional **players iron** usually prioritises compact shaping, feedback and workability. It may offer less help when contact moves away from the centre.

A **game-improvement iron** usually uses a larger head, wider sole, more offset or other design features intended to help launch and forgiveness. It can inspire confidence for a golfer who values assistance over a compact look.

A **players-distance iron** sits between those ideas. It aims to retain a refined shape while using hollow construction, thin faces, internal weighting or flexible face structures to create speed and protect more ball speed on imperfect contact.

These are market categories, not regulated performance grades. Always compare the actual specifications and your shot pattern.

## Why the P790 is called players distance

TaylorMade’s own comparison describes the 2025 P790 as:

- Players-distance style.
- Mid-high forgiveness.
- Mid-high trajectory.
- Mid workability.
- Long distance.

In the same comparison, its game-improvement models sit higher for forgiveness and trajectory, while the more compact P770, P7CB, P7MB and P7TW move progressively toward workability. That positioning explains the intended P790 buyer: a golfer who wants a players-inspired profile without moving fully into a less-forgiving compact iron.

## How the hollow-body construction works

The P790 is not a simple one-piece blade. It uses a hollow-body architecture that lets the face and internal structure be engineered separately. The cavity creates room for face flexibility, internal mass placement and TaylorMade’s SpeedFoam Air material.

Hollow construction can support speed and forgiveness while preserving a slimmer external profile. It can also change sound and feel, which is why manufacturers use internal structures and fillers to tune impact.

Do not confuse “hollow body” with “empty” or “fragile.” It describes the construction method. Condition, authenticity and specification still need to be checked like any other premium club.

## What does a forged face mean?

TaylorMade states that the 2025 P790 uses a 4340M forged face material and says it is 20% stronger than the previous generation. A stronger face material can allow engineers to design face geometry around speed and durability targets.

The word forged applies to the face; it does not mean the whole head is a traditional one-piece forged blade. That distinction matters when comparing feel claims or shopping descriptions. Use the complete phrase: forged-face hollow-body iron.

Feel remains subjective. Ball type, shaft, grip and strike location also influence what reaches your hands and ears.

## What is SpeedFoam Air?

SpeedFoam Air is TaylorMade’s internal material used within the hollow head. The manufacturer says it supports face performance while helping tune sound and feel.

It is best understood as one part of the system. It does not independently create distance, and a product name cannot tell you how the club will feel to you. Hit shots if possible and compare centred and off-centre contact.

## What is FLTD CG?

FLTD CG is TaylorMade’s term for moving centre-of-gravity placement progressively through the iron set. The long irons are designed with a lower centre of gravity to support launch, while the centre moves higher through the shorter irons for flight and control.

This approach recognises that a 4-iron and pitching wedge should not solve the same problem. The long iron needs speed and launch; the scoring club needs predictable distance and trajectory.

The Karibu set runs from 20° in the 4-iron to 44° in the pitching wedge. Read our [4–PW set guide](/blog/4-pw-iron-set-explained/) for the complete loft progression and wedge-gap questions.

## How does sole design affect play?

TaylorMade describes an increased sole radius and progressive leading edge for improved turf interaction and impact location. The sole is the part of the head that contacts the ground, so its width, curvature, bounce and leading edge can influence how the club enters and exits the turf.

No sole design works identically for every swing and surface. A steep delivery on soft ground presents different challenges from a shallow delivery on firm turf. Evaluate strike and turf interaction rather than assuming “players shape” means difficult or “wide sole” means easy.

## Does stronger loft automatically mean more distance?

The 2025 P790 7-iron is 30°. Loft is one ingredient in distance, but speed, launch, spin and strike determine the actual result. A lower number on a launch monitor is not always better if the ball cannot hold a green.

When testing players-distance irons, measure:

1. Carry rather than total distance alone.
2. Peak height and landing behaviour.
3. Front-to-back consistency.
4. Left-to-right dispersion.
5. Distance loss on normal misses.
6. Gaps between neighbouring clubs.

The longest single shot is poor evidence. A useful iron produces a repeatable window.

## Who may benefit from players-distance irons?

This category may suit a golfer who wants:

- A less bulky look at address.
- More speed support than a compact one-piece players iron.
- A blend of forgiveness and workable flight.
- Long-iron help without moving to the largest game-improvement profile.
- A premium iron set that can remain useful as ball striking develops.

A different category may be better if you need the highest possible launch and forgiveness, dislike a compact head, or want maximum feedback and shot-shaping in a smaller players iron.

## How to evaluate a P790 set in Kenya

Use the technology as a shortlist, then verify the item:

- Confirm it is the intended model year.
- Check all seven 4–PW clubs.
- Confirm steel or graphite shaft, model, weight and flex.
- Confirm handedness, length and any alterations.
- Request photographs of the actual heads, faces, soles, shafts and grips.
- Compare the current KSh price with the exact delivered configuration.
- Ask about delivery and seller terms before payment.

The [Karibu P790 product page](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) combines current stock, KSh price, photographs, specifications and a configuration enquiry. The team confirms the exact product through WhatsApp before the order is finalised.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are players-distance irons the same as blades?

No. They may have a blade-like appearance, but many use hollow bodies, thin faces and internal weighting for speed and forgiveness.

### Are P790 irons forgiving?

TaylorMade rates them mid-high for forgiveness within its iron comparison. They are not positioned as the company’s maximum-forgiveness option. Your own strike pattern should decide.

### Is the 2025 P790 fully forged?

TaylorMade describes a forged 4340M face in a hollow-body head. It should not be described as a traditional one-piece forged blade.

### What handicap should use P790 irons?

There is no official handicap requirement. Golfers with the same handicap can have very different speed and contact patterns. Test launch, dispersion and gapping instead.
